title: connection
description: An external service: where user tokens may be sent, what they look like, and how users authorize.

hosts.description: Host names the user token may be sent to, matched exactly. An entry written as host/path/ admits only requests below that path, for hosts that serve unrelated APIs side by side.

base_url.description: Root URL of the service when it differs per installation, such as GitHub Enterprise or a tenant subdomain. Its host is added to hosts, and it replaces {base_url} wherever the connection's URLs are written around it.

redirect_hosts.description: Host names a download may be redirected to, matched exactly. The user token never travels to them.

token_prefixes.description: Prefixes of issued tokens. Empty means the service does not announce itself and tokens are accepted by elimination; an agent may declare only one such connection.

scopes.description: Scope to the explanation shown on the consent screen. Every agent that declares the connection gets these.

optional_scopes.description: Scope to the explanation shown on the consent screen. The menu an agent may select from; none of these reach a token unless the agent declares them.

pkce.description: Whether the authorization server is to be sent a code challenge. Some refuse a code exchange without one.

authorization_query.description: Query string for the authorization URL, used verbatim. Gemini Enterprise adds client_id and redirect_uri.

oauth_client.description: Prefix of the Secret Manager secrets holding the OAuth client: <prefix>-client-id and <prefix>-client-secret.

setup.description: What a person has to do before anyone can authorize: register the OAuth client, what the consent screen grants, anything that cannot be undone. gete can neither do nor check any of it; `gete connections <id>` prints it.

retired.description: Why the connection is no longer usable. validate fails with this text.

examples.description: Shapes of tokens, not real ones. The catalog checks accepts_token against them.

messages.description: Texts shown to end users, in the installation's language.

reauthorization.description: Shown when the user's token is missing or unusable and they have to approve the connection again.

rooted_url.description: An https URL, or one written around {base_url} when the service's root differs per installation. The placeholder stands for the whole root and appears once, at the front; a catalog entry that spelled half a host, or tucked the root elsewhere into the URL, would let whatever fills it decide part of the name.
